What the spooler queue shows

The header line gives the collection point: 26 Oct 2026 07:11:50, and the queue is titled "Spooler Queue Elements".

The report closes with a native total: 64 Queue Elements. 180 Frames in use.

What this establishes
The print spooler (the D3 queue that holds formatted output awaiting a printer device) has 64 queued elements owned by user dm, totaling 180 frames of spool space — that's a native total from the report, not a derived count.
Every visible entry shares the same status token C880, the same form 100, and 1 copy, and the same queue/link number 27, so this looks like one device/queue stream rather than mixed destinations.
All visible entries are stamped September 3–6, 2026, while the report itself ran in late October — i.e., these entries are weeks old and still in the queue. I'd call that inference, not proof of a stuck printer; a full printer-device read is needed to say whether the device is active, disabled, or holding.
Caveats (important)
The tool output was truncated — 56 lines omitted. So the rows I quoted and the trailing 64 Queue Elements total are the reliable anchors; I cannot vouch for the middle entries, nor can I infer anything about jobs or printers that would appear outside this queue listing.
Queue elements existing does not mean printing is happening; only the queue side was read. No printer device status or print-queue job detail was inspected, and nothing was stopped, printed, or cancelled.

Want me to follow up read-only with area: printers (device status) to see whether the 27 device behind these 64 entries is online or backed up?
